rationale: The expected positive sign contradicts the well-documented negative capex/investment anomaly (Titman-Wei-Xie), and the hard INDICATOR gate collapses all negative-cash-flow firms to a single zero value so the short leg becomes a distress/loss-firm basket rather than a "low-quality investment" basket, making the test uninterpretable as stated.

This is a mechanical product of two of the most heavily published anomalies (Cooper-Gulen-Schill asset growth and Sloan accruals) that are themselves near-redundant by construction — accruals are a component of asset growth — so the interaction adds essentially no information beyond the known overlap documented by Fairfield-Whisenant-Yohn and Wu-Zhang-Zhang.

The acquirer-quality conditioning is a defensible and not-yet-standard interaction with a sign consistent with the expression, but aqc is zero or missing for most firm-years, so the rank has massive ties and the multiplicative form means the spread will be driven by a thin acquiring subsample — coverage and portfolio-stability diagnostics must be scrutinized.

The components are individually published (inventory growth; Novy-Marx gross profitability scaled by assets), but the specific "unproductive working-capital build at low-margin firms" interaction is coherent, sign-consistent with the expression, and has broad coverage, so it is worth testing while acknowledging much of the alpha may be inherited from the standalone legs.

The construction is internally muddled — it blends a component with a documented negative return relation (capex intensity) with one implying a positive relation (low earnings volatility) while asserting a positive sign — and dividing by a 5-period earnings volatility that can be near zero produces an explosive, non-monotone variable that 1% winsorization will not tame.

The mechanism is reasonable, but a product of two ranks is a monotone blend rather than a gate, so the signal will likely inherit the well-documented negative hiring-rate premium (Belo-Lin-Bazdresch) and thus contradict the stated positive expected sign; a genuine conditional form (e.g., hiring growth only among improving-margin firms, contrasted with hiring among deteriorating-margin firms) would be needed to test the hypothesis.
